In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the minimal structure of an adjuvant-active lipoprotein is a tetrapeptide with the following sequence: L Ala→D isoglu→ L,D Dap←Glu, the carboxyl terminal of the glutamic acid being linked to the amino terminal of the D,D,L,L 2,6 diamino pimelate.
the minimal adjuvanticity is not a property of the sugar moiety but rather of the peptide backbone.
the lipopetide, L-Ala→D-Glu→L,L-Dap←Gly, is the minimal immunostimulating adjuvant structure of bacterial cell-wall peptidoglycan.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the immunostimulating activities of the lipopeptide were found to be independent of its chemical coupling to the muramic acid residue of the peptidoglycan.
we have shown that the immunopotentiating effect of the cell walls is not dependent upon the presence of the sugar component of the cell walls, i.e., muramic acid.
a lipopeptide of the formula: N-acyl- L ala- D iso-Glu- L,D-Dap-Gly is a new immunostimulant and that it is as effective as MDP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sugar moiety of bacterial cell walls is not essential for the immunopotentiating activity of these molecules, and that the lipid moiety can be replaced by a fatty acid chain.
the presence of sugar in the structure of immunostimulatory molecules is not an absolute requirement for immunopotentiator activity.
